topics.title: Types of Banks and Major Functions
explain: India has various banking institutions tailored to specific economic sectors and customer groups.
Commercial Banks are widespread and cater to the general public, trade, and industry.
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) serve financial requirements in rural regions.
Co-operative Banks function on cooperative principles under state or multi-state acts.
Payment Banks accept restricted deposits but cannot issue credit cards or extend loans.
Development Banks finance infrastructure projects, while Small Finance Banks serve unorganised sectors.
The two fundamental functions of commercial banks are accepting deposits and granting advances.

flow.title: Core Operating Cycle of Commercial Banks

topics.example: A customer deposits ₹1,00,000 in a savings account at 3% interest, and the bank lends that money to a small business owner at 9% interest. The 6% difference is the spread.
remember: Payment Banks CANNOT issue loans or credit cards.
The difference between interest earned on advances and interest paid on deposits is called 'Spread'.
mistakes: Assuming Payment Banks can issue credit cards or extend term loans.

quiz.q: Which type of bank is permitted to accept restricted deposits but prohibited from issuing loans and credit cards?
quiz.why: As per RBI guidelines, Payment Banks can accept restricted deposits but cannot grant loans or issue credit cards.

quiz.q: What constitutes the core financial spread of a commercial bank?
o: Commission on locker rentals minus IT costs
Interest charged on advances minus interest paid on deposits
Processing fees earned minus salary paid to staff
Profit on sale of investments minus brokerage charges
quiz.why: The spread is the difference between the higher interest rate charged on advances and the lower interest rate paid on deposits.

topics.title: Regulatory Framework and RBI Rules
explain: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank responsible for supervising and regulating the Indian banking system.
RBI determines monetary and credit policies in consultation with the Central Government.
No entity can start a banking business or open new branches without securing a license from the RBI.
RBI holds statutory powers to conduct inspections of any bank's operational and financial books.
Key governing enactments include the Banking Regulation Act 1949, State Bank of India Act 1955, Companies Act 2013, and RRB Act 1976.
topics.example: Before opening a new physical branch in a tier-2 city, a nationalized bank must seek prior approval and licensing from the Reserve Bank of India.
remember: Licensing and inspection powers rest strictly with the Reserve Bank of India.
Banking Regulation Act, 1949 is the foundational legislative enactment for bank regulations.
mistakes: Believing that a bank can open new branches freely without RBI approval.

quiz.q: Which authority holds the regulatory power to issue banking licenses and inspect bank operations in India?
o: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India
quiz.why: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the supreme regulatory body entrusted with licensing and inspecting banks.

quiz.q: Which of the following Acts acts as the main regulatory framework governing banking companies in India?
quiz.why: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 is the principal statutory enactment governing banking operations in India.

topics.title: Peculiarities of Bank Audit & Key Audit Reports
explain: Bank audits involve high volume and complexity of transactions, widespread branch networks, and heavy reliance on IT.
Statutory Central Auditors (SCAs) issue additional reports along with the main audit report.
The Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) must be submitted to the bank management by 30th June every year.
Additional reports cover SLR compliance, internal financial controls (IFC), treasury operations, NPA provisioning, and committee recommendations (Ghosh & Jilani).
Adverse credit-deposit ratios in rural areas and serious operational irregularities require explicit reporting.

flow.title: Reporting Obligations of Statutory Central Auditor

topics.example: The central statutory auditor finishes branch audits and compiles the Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) detailing internal control defects, submitting it by 30th June.
remember: LFAR submission deadline: 30th June every year.
Reports on Ghosh (frauds) and Jilani (internal controls) committee recommendations are mandatory.
mistakes: Confusing the submission deadline of LFAR with standard income tax filing deadlines.

quiz.q: What is the statutory deadline for Statutory Central Auditors to submit the Long Form Audit Report (LFAR) to the bank?
quiz.why: Statutory Central Auditors are required to submit the LFAR to the bank management latest by 30th June every year.

quiz.q: Which committee's recommendations focus specifically on internal control and credit inspection systems in banks?
quiz.why: The Jilani Committee recommendations relate specifically to internal control and inspection/credit systems.

topics.title: Bank Audit Approach and Engagement Team Discussions
explain: Audit planning depends on operational scale, adverse features, past compliance, and assessed internal control risks.
Auditors must evaluate the bank's control environment covering segregation of duties between front office and back office.
Core questions to evaluate controls: Who, What, When, Where, Why, and How.
Engagement Team Discussions (ETD) must take place at the planning stage between partner and team members.
ETD focuses on fraud susceptibility, prior year errors, professional skepticism, and audit responses to specific risks.

flow.title: Steps in Developing Bank Audit Approach

topics.example: During the planning meeting, the audit partner discusses with assistants how front-office staff might bypass CBS security controls, setting specific test checks for unauthorized manual entries.
remember: ETD must occur primarily at the planning stage of the audit.
Front office (dealing/trade) and back office (accounting/settlement) duties must be strictly segregated.
mistakes: Assuming engagement team discussions can be omitted if team members audited the same branch last year.

quiz.q: At what stage of the audit assignment should Engagement Team Discussions ideally be conducted?
o: At the planning stage of the audit
After issuing the main audit report
At the time of submitting the LFAR
quiz.why: Engagement team discussions are ordinarily conducted at the planning stage to assess risk of material misstatements.

quiz.q: Effective internal control in bank dealing room operations mandates strict segregation between which two functions?
quiz.why: Proper internal controls require segregation between front office (transaction execution) and back office (settlement & accounting).

topics.title: Form, Content of Financial Statements & Audit of Accounts
explain: Section 29 of Banking Regulation Act 1949 mandates every bank to prepare Balance Sheet (Form A) and P&L (Form B) as per Third Schedule.
These forms apply to banking companies, nationalized banks, State Bank of India, and Regional Rural Banks.
Banks must comply with Accounting Standards specified under Section 133 of Companies Act 2013.
Section 30(1) requires financial statements to be audited by a person qualified under law to be a company auditor.
Unaudited branch details (advances, deposits, interest income/expense) must be quantified and disclosed in the central audit report.

flow.title: Financial Statement Preparation and Audit Mandate

topics.example: A nationalized bank prepares its balance sheet in Form A of the Third Schedule and discloses the total deposits and advances of its 50 unaudited rural branches directly in the auditor's report.
remember: Form A = Balance Sheet; Form B = Profit and Loss Account (Third Schedule).
Auditor must quantify advances, deposits, interest income, and interest expenses of unaudited branches in the audit report.
mistakes: Thinking that nationalized banks use standard Schedule III format of Companies Act 2013 instead of Third Schedule of Banking Regulation Act 1949.

quiz.q: Which schedule and forms of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 prescribe the layout of financial statements for banks?
o: Third Schedule - Form A & Form B
Schedule III - Part I & Part II
Fourth Schedule - Form X & Form Y
quiz.why: Form A (Balance Sheet) and Form B (P&L Account) of the Third Schedule to the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 prescribe the format.

quiz.q: What specific operational data regarding unaudited branches must be explicitly quantified and disclosed in the bank audit report?
o: Advances, deposits, interest income, and interest expense
IT infrastructure expenses and AMC costs
quiz.why: Quantification of advances, deposits, interest income, and interest expense for unaudited branches must be disclosed in the report.

topics.title: Auditor Appointment, Powers, CARO Exemption & RBI Reporting
explain: Banking Company Auditor: Appointed at AGM by shareholders with prior RBI approval.
Nationalized Bank Auditor: Appointed by Board of Directors with prior RBI approval.
RRB Auditor: Appointed by the bank concerned with Central Government approval.
Remuneration: Fixed under Sec 142 of Companies Act for banking companies; fixed by RBI in consultation with Central Govt for Nationalized Banks/SBI.
CARO 2020 is NOT applicable to any banking company defined under Section 5(c) of Banking Regulation Act 1949.
Auditors must report frauds or foul play to RBI as per RBI Circular, overriding confidentiality (SA 250 & SA 240).
topics.example: When appointing statutory auditors for a nationalized bank, the Board of Directors sends the proposed names to the RBI for prior approval before finalizing the appointment.
remember: CARO 2020 does NOT apply to banking companies.
Statutory audit firms CANNOT take up internal/concurrent audit assignments in the same bank during the same year.
Reporting fraud to RBI overrides duty of confidentiality under SA 250.
mistakes: Applying CARO 2020 reporting requirements to bank audit reports.
Assuming a firm can perform both concurrent audit and statutory central audit of the same bank in the same year.

quiz.q: Which of the following reporting orders is strictly NOT applicable to a banking company?
quiz.why: CARO 2020 is explicitly non-applicable to banking companies as defined in Section 5(c) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

quiz.q: Who appoints statutory central auditors in the case of a nationalized bank?
o: Bank's Board of Directors with prior approval of RBI
Central Government with approval of ICAI
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
quiz.why: Auditors of nationalized banks are appointed by the bank's Board of Directors with prior approval of the RBI.

topics.title: Conducting an Audit: Stages, IT System & Risk Management
explain: Auditors must submit a declaration of indebtedness before accepting appointment.
Auditor must send written communication and obtain No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the previous auditor (Clause 8, Part I, 1st Schedule, CA Act 1949).
Auditor must perform procedures under SA 300, SA 220, SA 210, SA 510 (Opening Balances), and SA 315.
In computerized CBS environments, auditors must check parameters built into IT systems using Professional Skepticism without assuming system data is error-free.
Commercial banks must put in place a Board-approved 'Stress Testing Framework' and adhere to Basel III capital adequacy norms.
topics.example: The incoming auditor writes a registered letter to the outgoing auditor seeking NOC and checks whether CBS software automatically flags accounts as NPA on day 91.
remember: System-generated reports cannot be trusted blindly; manual validation is required.
Stress Testing Framework must be Board-approved as mandated by RBI.
Basel III norms are set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS).
mistakes: Assuming IT automated NPA classification requires no independent verification by the auditor.

quiz.q: What professional standard requires the auditor to communicate in writing with the previous auditor to obtain an NOC?
o: Clause (8) of Part I of First Schedule to CA Act, 1949
quiz.why: Clause (8) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 mandates prior written communication with the retiring auditor.

quiz.q: What software testing methodology is mandated by RBI for commercial banks to assess system resilience under extreme conditions?
quiz.why: RBI mandates that all commercial banks put in place a Board-approved Stress Testing framework integrated into risk management.

topics.title: Advances: Types and Modes of Creation of Security
explain: Funded Loans involve actual money transfer (Term Loans, Cash Credits, Overdrafts, Demand Loans, Bills Discounted).
Non-Funded Facilities do not involve immediate cash outflow (Letters of Credit, Bank Guarantees).
Primary Security is the principal security offered for the facility (e.g., stocks, raw materials).
Collateral Security is additional security provided (e.g., land, buildings).
Mortgage: Registered (via Mortgage Deed) or Equitable (delivery of title deeds).
Pledge: Transfer of possession/bailment of goods; legal ownership remains with pledger.
Hypothecation: Equitable charge on moveable goods without transfer of ownership or possession.
Assignment: Transfer of actionable claims (e.g., book debts, life insurance policies).
Set-off: Statutory right to combine debit and credit accounts of the same customer in same capacity.
Lien: Legal right to retain goods/securities until debt is discharged.

flow.title: Modes of Charge Creation on Securities

topics.example: A factory owner takes a Cash Credit loan by pledging stock stored in a bank-locked warehouse, hypothecating machinery inside the factory, and depositing title deeds of land as an equitable mortgage.
remember: Hypothecation: Possession stays with borrower as agent/trustee.
Pledge: Possession is delivered to the bank.
Set-off applies across all branches of the same bank for accounts in the same name and same right.
mistakes: Confusing Hypothecation with Pledge regarding who holds physical possession of the goods.

quiz.q: Which mode of security creation involves delivery of title deeds with intent to create security without a registered deed?
quiz.why: Equitable mortgage is effected simply by delivering title deeds or documents of title to the bank.

quiz.q: How does Hypothecation differ fundamentally from a Pledge?
o: Hypothecation transfers ownership while pledge does not.
Pledge involves physical delivery of goods to bank, whereas hypothecation does not.
Hypothecation is used only for real estate, pledge for moveables.
Pledge is non-funded while hypothecation is funded.
quiz.why: Pledge involves bailment/possession of goods to the bank, while hypothecation creates a charge on moveable goods retaining possession with the borrower.

topics.title: Prudential Norms: NPA, Out of Order & Overdue Concepts
explain: Non-Performing Asset (NPA): An asset that stops generating income for the bank.
Term Loans: Interest/principal installment remains overdue for > 90 days.
Bills Discounted: Bill remains overdue for > 90 days.
Overdraft / Cash Credit: Account remains 'Out of Order'.

Out of Order Definition: Outstanding balance continuously exceeds sanctioned limit/drawing power; OR balance is within limit but no credits for 90 days as on Balance Sheet date; OR credits are insufficient to cover interest debited during the period.
Overdue Definition: Any amount due to the bank is not paid on the due date fixed by the bank.
NPA classification is based strictly on record of recovery, regardless of security or net worth of guarantor.

flow.title: NPA Identification Test (Term Loan vs CC/OD)
steps: CC / OD: Is Account Out of Order?
If YES to any -> Classify as NPA

topics.example: A CC borrower has a sanctioned limit of ₹50 Lakhs. Interest debited during the quarter is ₹3 Lakhs, but total credits deposited are only ₹50,000. The account is 'Out of Order' and thus an NPA.
remember: NPA benchmark for term loans & bills = > 90 days overdue.
Security availability or guarantor net worth CANNOT prevent an account from becoming an NPA if recovery is overdue.
mistakes: Thinking an account is safe from NPA status because the guarantor has high net worth.

quiz.q: A Cash Credit account balance is within sanctioned limits, but no credit entries are recorded for 90 days continuously as on balance sheet date. What is the status of the account?
quiz.why: No credits continuously for 90 days in an operating account renders it 'out of order' and consequently an NPA.

quiz.q: Can an advance overdue for 120 days be kept as Standard Asset if the borrower provides high-value collateral security?
o: No, NPA classification depends on record of recovery, not availability of security.
Yes, if approved by statutory central auditor.
quiz.why: Availability of security or net worth of borrower/guarantor is irrelevant for treating an advance as NPA.

topics.title: Asset Classification Categories and Provisioning Rules
explain: Standard Assets: regular or showing stress (SMA 0: 1-30 days, SMA 1: 31-60 days, SMA 2: 61-90 days overdue).
Substandard Assets: NPA for period <= 12 months. Provision required: 15% (on total balance).
Doubtful Assets: Remained in Substandard category for > 12 months.
Sub-categories of Doubtful Assets:
- D1 (up to 1 year): 25% secured + 100% unsecured.
- D2 (1 to 3 years): 40% secured + 100% unsecured.
- D3 (> 3 years): 100% secured + 100% unsecured.
Loss Assets: Loss identified by bank, auditor, or RBI inspection, but not written off. Provision required: 100%.
Critical Principle: Asset classification is BORROWER-WISE, not facility-wise. If one facility turns NPA, all facilities of that borrower turn NPA.
topics.example: Mr. A has a home loan (regular) and a car loan (overdue 100 days) with the same bank. Because classification is borrower-wise, BOTH home loan and car loan are classified as NPA.
remember: Asset classification is BORROWER-WISE.
Substandard provision = 15%.
Doubtful Secured Provisions: D1 = 25%, D2 = 40%, D3 = 100%.
Unsecured portion of Doubtful Asset ALWAYS requires 100% provision.
mistakes: Classifying one loan of a borrower as Standard and another as NPA (facility-wise mistake).
Applying 25% or 40% provision on the unsecured portion of a Doubtful Asset instead of 100%.

quiz.q: If a borrower defaults on a car loan (NPA), while their housing loan with the same bank is paid regularly, how should the housing loan be classified?
quiz.why: Asset classification is borrower-wise, not facility-wise. All facilities of the borrower become NPA.

quiz.q: What is the required provision percentage for the SECURED portion of a Doubtful advance in the D2 category (doubtful for 1 to 3 years)?
quiz.why: Doubtful D2 category (1 to 3 years) requires a provision of 40% on the secured portion and 100% on the unsecured portion.

topics.title: Special Categories of Advances & Rules
explain: Accounts Regularized Near Balance Sheet Date: Window-dressing transactions near 31st March (e.g., quick deposit and immediate April reversal) must be checked. Weak accounts should be treated as NPA.
Central Government Guaranteed Advances: Classified as Standard for provisioning, but treated as NPA for Income Recognition if overdue > 90 days, until guarantee is invoked/repudiated.
State Government Guaranteed Advances: Treated as NPA for BOTH provisioning and income recognition if overdue > 90 days.
Erosion of Security: Realizable security value < 50% of last assessed value -> Straight to Doubtful; Realizable security value < 10% of outstanding balance -> Straight to Loss Asset (100% provision).
Advances against Term Deposits/NSCs/KVPs: Need not be treated as NPA if adequate margin is available.
Agricultural Advances: Short-duration crops -> NPA if overdue for 2 crop seasons; Long-duration crops -> NPA if overdue for 1 crop season.

flow.title: Erosion of Security Test
steps: If YES -> Straight to LOSS ASSET (100%)
If NO: Is Security < 50% of Last Value?
If YES -> Straight to DOUBTFUL ASSET

topics.example: A loan of ₹10 Crore has security whose valuation drops to ₹80 Lakhs (less than 10% of ₹10 Crore). The auditor ignores security and straight-away classifies it as a Loss Asset.
remember: Central Govt Guarantee: Standard for provisioning (until invoked/repudiated), NPA for income recognition.
State Govt Guarantee: NPA for both provisioning and income recognition if > 90 days overdue.
Agricultural: Short crop = 2 seasons overdue; Long crop = 1 season overdue.
mistakes: Treating Central Govt and State Govt guarantees identically for NPA provisioning.
Gradually downgrading an account to substandard when security value has eroded below 10%.

quiz.q: An advance guaranteed by the State Government remains overdue for 120 days. How should it be treated?
o: Standard Asset for both income and provisioning
NPA for both Provisioning and Income Recognition
NPA for Income Recognition only, Standard for Provisioning
quiz.why: State Govt guaranteed advances overdue for > 90 days are treated as NPA for both provisioning and income recognition.

quiz.q: If the realizable value of security falls below 10% of the outstanding loan balance, how should the asset be classified?
quiz.why: When security value is less than 10% of outstanding loan balance, security is ignored and asset is straight-away classified as Loss Asset.

topics.title: Computation of Drawing Power & Stock Audit
explain: Drawing Power (DP) is the maximum operational limit up to which a borrower can withdraw within the sanctioned limit for Cash Credit facilities.
DP = (Realisable Value of Eligible Primary Stocks + Debtors) minus Unpaid Stocks (Creditors) minus Stipulated Margins.
Stock Statements older than 3 months cannot be relied upon; drawings based on older statements are deemed irregular.
Stock Audit is mandatory for all borrower accounts having funded exposure exceeding ₹5 Crores.
Sundry creditors for goods must be deducted from gross stock before applying margin.

flow.title: Calculation Steps for Drawing Power
steps: Total Stock DP + Debtor DP = Final DP

topics.example: Gross stocks ₹100L, damaged stocks ₹10L, creditors ₹20L. Paid stock = ₹70L. With 25% margin, stock DP is ₹52.5L. Adding debtor DP gives total DP.
remember: Stock statements older than 3 months make the account irregular.
Stock audit threshold: Funded exposure > ₹5 Crores.
Creditors for goods MUST be deducted to arrive at paid stock before applying margin.
mistakes: Applying margin percentage on total gross stocks without deducting unpaid stock (creditors).

quiz.q: Stock statements relied upon by banks for computing Drawing Power must not be older than how many months?
quiz.why: Stock statements older than 3 months cannot be used for calculating drawing power; drawings based on them are irregular.

quiz.q: A bank must conduct a mandatory stock audit for borrower accounts exceeding what funded exposure threshold?
quiz.why: Stock audit by external professionals is mandatory for accounts with funded exposure exceeding ₹5 Crores.

topics.title: Audit of Advances and Evaluation of Internal Controls
explain: Auditors examine large advances thoroughly, while other advances can be checked on a sample basis.
A 'Large Advance' is defined as year-end balance > ₹10 Crores or 10% of aggregate branch advances, whichever is less.
Auditors verify existence, enforceability, and valuation of security, loan documentation, and sanction compliance.
Internal Control Checks: Creditworthiness checks before sanction, execution of promissory notes/hypothecation agreements prior to disbursement, end-use of funds, DP register updating.
Operations in advance accounts must be reviewed at least once a year.
topics.example: At a branch with total advances of ₹80 Crores, 10% is ₹8 Crores. Since ₹8 Crores is less than ₹10 Crores, any advance exceeding ₹8 Crores is classified as a large advance and examined in detail.
remember: Large Advance Benchmark: > ₹10 Crores OR 10% of branch total advances, WHICHEVER IS LESS.
Every advance account operation must be reviewed at least once a year.
mistakes: Taking ₹10 Crores as a fixed limit for large advances without comparing it with 10% of total branch advances.

quiz.q: What constitutes a 'large advance' at a branch with aggregate year-end advances of ₹60 Crores?
quiz.why: Large advance is > ₹10 Crore or 10% of aggregate advances, whichever is less. 10% of ₹60 Cr is ₹6 Cr, which is lower.

quiz.q: How frequently should the operations of each advance account at a bank branch be reviewed at minimum?
o: At least once every two years
Only when the account becomes NPA
quiz.why: Bank internal control guidelines require the operation of each advance account to be reviewed at least once a year.

topics.title: Audit of Revenue Items: Income and Reversal Rules
explain: Income is generally recognized on accrual basis if ultimate collection is reasonably certain.
Income from Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) CANNOT be recognized on accrual basis; it is booked ONLY on actual cash receipt basis.
Reversal of Income: When an account turns NPA, all accrued but unrealized interest credited in past periods must be reversed or provided for.
Fees, commission, and leased asset finance income accrued on NPAs must also be stopped and reversed if uncollected.
Materiality Policy (RBI): Any income item > 1% of total gross income (or > 1% of net profit before tax if net) must be accrued as per AS 9.
Memorandum Account: Interest accrued on NPAs post-classification is recorded off-balance sheet in a Memorandum Account for control.

flow.title: Income Recognition & Reversal Flow for NPAs
steps: Record Subsequent Interest in Memorandum A/c
Recognize Income ONLY on Cash Receipt

topics.example: When a corporate loan turns NPA on 31st December, the bank reverses ₹15 Lakhs of interest accrued and credited to P&L during previous quarters that remains uncollected.
remember: NPA Income Recognition = CASH / RECEIPT BASIS ONLY.
Interest in Memorandum Account is NOT added to Gross Advances on Balance Sheet.
mistakes: Accruing interest on an NPA account because strong collateral is available.

quiz.q: How must income from Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) be recognized in bank financial statements?
quiz.why: Due to significant uncertainty of recovery, income on NPAs can only be recognized when actually realized in cash.

quiz.q: What accounting entry is required for interest previously accrued and credited to income when an advance becomes an NPA?
o: Capitalize it into borrower's loan balance
Reverse or provide for the unrealized interest
quiz.why: Unrealized interest accrued in past periods for an account turning NPA must be reversed or fully provided for.

topics.title: Audit of Revenue Items: Expenses and Provisions
explain: Bank Expenditure is classified under three broad heads: (1) Interest Expense, (2) Operating Expenses, and (3) Provisions & Contingencies.
Interest Expenses: Automatically calculated via CBS batch process; auditor evaluates weighted average interest rates per quarter and tests sample computations.
Operating Expenses: Include employee payments, rent, lighting, audit fees, depreciation, IT costs. Auditor performs trend analysis and ratio analysis.
Provisions & Contingencies: Includes NPA provisions, tax provisions, diminution in investment values, and standard asset provisions.
Auditor procedures for provisions: Verify compliance with RBI circulars, reconcile GL balances, check tax computations, and test sample loan classifications.
topics.example: The auditor compares the average interest rate paid on savings deposits (3.5%) against quarterly general ledger figures and recalculates interest accruals for a sample of fixed deposit accounts.
remember: Three Heads of Expenses: Interest Expense, Operating Expenses, Provisions & Contingencies.
Interest calculation in modern banks is driven by CBS batch processing.
mistakes: Treating Provisions for NPAs or Taxes as Operating Expenses instead of under 'Provisions and Contingencies'.

quiz.q: Which head of expense includes provisions made for Non-Performing Assets and Income Tax in a bank's P&L account?
quiz.why: NPA provisions and tax provisions fall under the main head 'Provisions and Contingencies' in Form B.

quiz.q: What analytical audit procedure helps verify the overall reasonableness of interest expense on deposits?
o: Calculating ratio of total interest paid to average deposit liability
Comparing physical stock statements with cash balances
Verifying board resolution for staff welfare expenditure
Checking credit card fee income against merchant accounts
quiz.why: Comparing the weighted average rate of interest paid on deposits with actual average rates paid helps assess reasonableness.
